purpose: Acceptance scenarios for both the browser design reference and the production-rendered native test app; this file is a specification, not passing test evidence.

steps: Select a non-default row using mouse down
Refresh the model before mouse up
expect: The clicked stable resource key stays selected
Details and preview describe that key
Exactly one selection write occurs

steps: Filter so that row is absent
expect: Selection follows the documented hidden-selection policy
No unrelated row becomes selected
Visible count equals filtered source count

steps: Sort each column ascending and descending
expect: Selection follows stable key
Equal values use a deterministic key tie-breaker
Rows do not flicker across identical refreshes
Widget count is bounded by viewport plus overscan, not record count
Displayed cells and selection match current keys
Removed resources are released
Stable expansion and selected key survive refresh
Keyboard navigation reaches visible nodes
Category filter and table agree
Edit belongs to the original stable key
Apply emits one typed action
Invalid numeric input cannot mutate the model
Fields show the newly selected resource

steps: Resize through declared viewports and DPI scales
expect: No overlapping controls or unreachable clipped actions
Text wraps inside its allotted width
Splitter constraints and scroll boundaries are respected

steps: Select a table row and scroll
Resize splitter and switch details tab
expect: Focused leaf has the new ancestor path
Edit, selection, expansion, offsets, pane ratio and tab are retained
No synthetic edit action occurs

steps: Reload an invalid final node or missing typed binding
expect: Revision and all mounted regions stay unchanged
No factory or model-write callback runs for schema-invalid input
Diagnostic identifies source, node and property
Corrected files recover normally

steps: Register a custom graph widget with typed properties
expect: No parser or renderer edits are needed for registration
Values update through typed bindings
Ownership and teardown are explicit
Invalid registration rejects atomically
Scoped IDs do not collide
Values remain independent
Both instances receive styling
Recursive or oversized expansion rejects atomically

steps: Destroy the view owner while controls have focus
expect: No stale brush/resource access
No callbacks into destroyed owners
No retained world handles or leaked widgets
Fresh log contains no unexpected ensures, errors or script warnings
No editor-only dependencies
Every action is reachable with visible focus
Localized text renders and wraps
Runtime resources and teardown remain valid
